result.question: How has Nvidia's data center business contributed to its revenue growth across its last three fiscal years?
result.answer:
Nvidia's data center business has been the primary driver of its revenue growth across the last three fiscal years (FY2024, FY2025, and FY2026). The company's total revenue grew from $60.9 billion in FY2024 [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2024-01-28] to $130.5 billion in FY2025 [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2025-01-26] and then to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [xbrl:0001045810-26-000021:us-gaap:Revenues:2026-01-25].

**FY2024 (ended January 28, 2024):** Total revenue was $60.9 billion, up 126% from $26.97 billion in FY2023 [0001045810-24-000029:item-7-p011]. Data Center revenue for the third quarter of FY2024 alone was $14.51 billion, up 279% from a year ago [0001045810-23-000227:part-i--item-2-p008].

**FY2025 (ended January 26, 2025):** Total revenue was $130.5 billion, up 114% from $60.9 billion in FY2024 [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p010]. Revenue from Data Center computing grew 162%, driven primarily by demand for the Hopper computing platform, while Data Center networking grew 51%, driven by Ethernet for AI revenue including the Spectrum-X platform [0001045810-25-000023:item-7-p010]. For the first nine months of FY2025, Data Center revenue reached $79.6 billion, compared to $29.1 billion in the same period of FY2024 [0001045810-24-000316:part-i--item-1-p021].

**FY2026 (ended January 25, 2026):** Total revenue was $215.9 billion, up 65% from $130.5 billion in FY2025 [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p008]. The Compute & Networking segment generated $193.5 billion, up 67% year-on-year, driven by major platform shifts in accelerated computing and AI [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p008]. Revenue from Data Center computing grew 59%, driven by demand for the Blackwell computing platform, while Data Center networking grew 142%, driven by NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems and growth of Ethernet and InfiniBand platforms [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p008]. The company noted that Blackwell architectures represented the majority of Data Center revenue in FY2026 [0001045810-26-000021:item-7-p001].

Across all three fiscal years, the Data Center business—housed within the Compute & Networking segment—was consistently identified as the primary driver of revenue growth, fueled by demand for AI training and inference, large language models, and generative AI applications. The platform transitioned from Hopper (FY2024–FY2025) to Blackwell (FY2026), sustaining the growth trajectory.

### Retracted claims

The following claims could not be verified against their cited sources and were removed from the answer:
- The Compute & Networking segment generated $47.4 billion in revenue in FY2024, up 215% year-on-year, driven by higher Data Center revenue from Compute GPU shipments of the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform.
- The Compute & Networking segment generated $116.2 billion in FY2025, up 145% year-on-year, driven by strong demand for accelerated computing and AI solutions.
